the radiotherapy field is advancing in terms of the treatment de intensification of cancer patients.
radiotherapy can be safely de intensified in elderly cancer patients, and that this is a feasible strategy to reduce the risk of overtreatment.
the radiotherapy of elderly patients should be personalized, taking into account the individual characteristics of each patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving quality of life and reducing treatment related morbidity in older cancer patients.
the development of a new model of oncologic care for elderly patients that is based on a multidisciplinary approach and the creation of oncologic coordination units.
the development of new strategies in radiation oncology for older patients, which are safe, effective, and feasible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
radiotherapy can be delivered safely and effectively in the elderly population with acceptable toxicity and efficacy.
the treatment of cancer in elderly patients should be individualized according to the patient’s comorbidity, functional status and life expectancy.
the use of radiotherapy in the elderly is feasible and safe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiotherapy of the elderly cancer patient should be based on a multidisciplinary approach and a geriatric evaluation.
the use of HF and ultra-HF regimens is a feasible strategy for elderly patients with prostate cancer, and SBRT may be an alternative to surgery for older patients with early stage NSCLC.
the de intensification of radiation therapy in older patients should be based on the individual patient and his or her comorbidities and functional status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
elderly cancer patients are significantly undertreated, and we need to change this situation.
radiotherapy in elderly patients is safe and feasible.
the de intensification of the radiation treatment in the elderly cancer patients is feasible, safe and should be considered as a standard approach.
